metadata.topic: AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all

theses.summary: AI demand is broadly accelerating across all major players in July-August 2026, contradicting public equity drawdowns
theses.detail: Baker asked every contact for one quantitative data point getting worse and found none. OpenAI accelerated, open source accelerated more, Grok/Grockbot had dramatic acceleration. Public AI stocks are in significant drawdowns despite fundamentals accelerating — a disconnect Baker views as an opportunity.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker states he asked 'everyone' and found zero negative data points; frames it as a personal high-conviction view held through summer 2026
theses.quote_fragment: public stocks have kind of fallen out of bed...things are broadly accelerating

theses.summary: The AI ecosystem is not zero-sum — frontier labs, open source, neoclouds, inference clouds, and applications can all win simultaneously
theses.detail: Baker explicitly rejects zero-sum framing. Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, Meta, Google (TPUs), open source, neoclouds, inference clouds, and well-executing application companies can all succeed. This is an 'and' not 'or' scenario.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'this is all wrong, this is not an or thing it's an and thing' and repeats it multiple times; frames it as his core LP-facing thesis
theses.quote_fragment: this is not an or thing it's an and thing

theses.summary: Frontier lab revenue is substantially self-determined by management decisions on compute allocation between training and inference, creating unusual public-market risk
theses.detail: Baker illustrates: a lab with 10GW allocating 8GW to inference at $60B/GW = $480B annualized revenue. If they shift to 8GW training, revenue drops to $120B. Labs would make this decision based on research breakthroughs. Revenue is also controlled by which checkpoint they release and where they price on the Pareto curve. This is structurally different from internet/cloud companies where revenue and infrastructure were decoupled.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker calls this something 'public markets are going to really have to get used to' and walks through specific numerical examples
theses.quote_fragment: a lot of the revenue is kind of under their control based on what checkpoint they release

theses.summary: Anthropic's quiet period revenue slowdown is likely accounting reclassification plus strategic timing ahead of IPO, not fundamental deceleration; next disclosure likely shows reacceleration
theses.detail: Baker hypothesizes Anthropic trued up accounting definitions to be comparable to OpenAI, then tested the waters. Given strong execution, he expects the next disclosure to show reacceleration. Anthropic is also strategically holding back model releases (e.g., waiting for OpenAI's Astra before releasing Claude 5.1) — competitive gamesmanship during IPO quiet period.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker explicitly labels this a 'hypothesis' but speaks with conviction based on pattern recognition
theses.quote_fragment: my hypothesis would be...probably the next disclosure is a reacceleration

theses.summary: Compute infrastructure paybacks are sub-one-year, making this one of the best capital deployment opportunities Baker has seen in his career
theses.detail: Nebius and Corweave disclosures imply 9-10 month payback: 1GW costs ~$50B, customers prepay 50-60% upfront (~$25-30B), remainder monetized at spot rates ($2-8/hr). SpaceX builds large clusters fast with even faster paybacks. True equity payback may be well inside one year. Nvidia GPUs are also financeable at low cost through Blackstone, KKR, Apollo — $50B data center requires only ~$15B equity check with $35B financed.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'in my career as an investor there haven't been that many opportunities where you have companies that could deploy tens hundreds of billions of dollars and get sub one-year paybacks'
theses.quote_fragment: sub one-year paybacks...I just in my career as an investor there haven't been that many opportunities

theses.summary: AI token demand is at extreme early innings — fewer than 10 million true heavy-paying users out of 1.5 billion knowledge workers; supply is massively constrained relative to addressable demand
theses.detail: Baker estimates fewer than 10M genuine heavy token consumers (taking the under on 30M). Power law within enterprises: highest-spending engineers use 10-100x median. AI-native a16z portfolio companies spend 10%+ of human compensation on tokens; old-economy leaders spend ~1%. Atreides internal token consumption up 100x from March to August 2026. Grockbot Enterprise access may 10-20x their spend in a single month.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker uses his own firm's data (100x token growth) and portfolio company data as primary evidence; speaks with high conviction
theses.quote_fragment: one and a half billion knowledge workers...we're nowhere on the demand side and we're massively supply constrained

theses.summary: Compute supply will be structurally undersupplied through at least 2028, driven by political/regulatory delays and fundamental material constraints
theses.detail: Baker states there is no available capacity with all forecast builds through 2028, and those builds are now likely delayed due to political dynamics. He is more worried about massive undersupply than overbuild. Copper, Watson wafers, and other raw materials are becoming binding constraints. Rising real rates and regulation compound the supply problem. This could lead to token price increases (Andreessen Horowitz cited a potential 10x token cost increase) rather than the consensus deflation narrative.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'Oh yeah. For through 28' without hedging; frames undersupply as his primary macro concern vs. consensus overbuild worry
theses.quote_fragment: everybody's worried about over supply. I'm more worried about massively under supply

theses.summary: Orbital/space-based compute is a credible and underappreciated solution to terrestrial compute supply constraints, with economics that flip favorably upon Starship reusability
theses.detail: SpaceX orbital data centers: roughly airplane-sized racks (~72 chips), sun-synchronous orbit with radiator in shadow for cooling. Cost breakdown: ~$35B of $50B/GW is chips (same as terrestrial), ~$15B is power/cooling/labor which is inflationary on Earth but near-zero in space (solar + radiator). With Starship reusability, launch cost drops below $1B, making orbital economics superior. Elon and Jensen co-designed a 'Rubin rack' launching Q4 2027 (call it 2028 with slippage). Baker views this as 'swing capacity' at minimum, potentially larger. Training will remain on Earth due to latency/interconnect requirements.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'it feels clear to me at a minimum it will be swing capacity' and walks through detailed cost math; dismisses physics objections by citing SpaceX engineering depth
theses.quote_fragment: an increasing fraction of the world's compute is going to be in orbit

theses.summary: SpaceX is a multi-trillion dollar opportunity even without orbital compute, via Starlink mobile (wireless + broadband ~$2T TAM), rapidly growing AI/AR revenue base, and cloud business
theses.detail: Starlink mobile addresses ~$800-900B wireless + broadband market, total ~$2T addressable. X ads are growing (Atreides has telemetry). Baker envisions a Starlink/Grockbot/X-advertising bundle analogous to Google bundling cloud with ads. Even in a scenario where SpaceX fumbles first-party AI applications, it remains a massive infrastructure business. Baker implies SpaceX is the first candidate for a $20T+ company.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'I know which one's going to be the first 20 trillion dollar company' (implied SpaceX); speaks without hedging on multiple revenue streams
theses.quote_fragment: I know which one's going to be the first 20 trillion dollar company

theses.summary: Nvidia is the central node of the entire AI ecosystem and its competitive moat is the financability of its data centers plus locked-up supply chain
theses.detail: Nvidia has locked up ~70-80% of world compute supply including fab capacity, DRAM, NAND, laser, capacitor, and rack components. Its data centers are the most financeable: $50B data center requires only $15B equity, $35B financed at low rates with RVG. TPUs are second-most financeable but require roughly double the equity check at higher rates. Jensen's strategy: vertically integrated but horizontally open (9 chip types). He is acquiring land, power, and shell companies and matchmaking with offtake agreements. RVGs help non-Anthropic/OpenAI players compete, democratizing compute and preventing AI concentration — aligned with US national interest.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'the last 26 years have taught me not to bet against Jensen' and provides detailed structural analysis of financing moat
theses.quote_fragment: Jensen's data centers are financeable...cost of capital is a huge advantage

theses.summary: The future of enterprise AI is a hybrid/multi-model architecture — own fine-tuned open-source model plus one or two frontier models behind a router — not a single dominant frontier model
theses.detail: Baker predicts enterprises will take the best open-source base model (likely an Nvidia model in the near future, given Poolside acquisition), do RL and supervised fine-tuning on proprietary data, then route to frontier models for planning while using the owned model for execution. This is good for Microsoft, application software companies, and Fireworks (Nexus product). Sharing proprietary enterprise context with frontier labs is 'hazardous for financial health' especially given ZDR policy shifts. Grockbot already uses Gemini 3.7 Flash + Grok 4.6 + Opus behind a router as a real-world example.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker calls this 'a very likely future to me' and cites multiple real-world instantiations (Grockbot, Cursor, Harvey, Fireworks Nexus)
theses.quote_fragment: the future is an ensemble of models...you want to own and control your intelligence

theses.summary: Nvidia is likely to release a competitive open-source frontier model, funded by its chip cash flows, potentially becoming the dominant American open-source model
theses.detail: Baker says 'in the very near future' the best open-source model will probably be an Nvidia model. Poolside acquisition was made for this reason — Poolside had strong American open-source talent. It is 'trivial' for Jensen to fund a $50-100B training run. Open source winning is good for Nvidia because lower margins on tokens = more token consumption = more compute demand. Google's long-term play may also be funding open-source training runs with TPU cash flows.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'I think probably in the very near near future that's going to be an NVIDIA model' — stated as expectation not certainty
theses.quote_fragment: in the very near future that's going to be an NVIDIA model

theses.summary: Microsoft is in a better strategic position than consensus believes, benefiting from the multi-model hybrid future even though it failed to build a competitive frontier model
theses.detail: Microsoft's 'specialized intelligence' strategy (Satya Nadella essay) is well-suited to a world where enterprises want owned fine-tuned models plus frontier routing. Microsoft can be the abstraction layer for enterprises. However, execution is extremely hard — competing with Databricks, Palantir, inference providers, application companies (Harvey, etc.), Salesforce, Workday, Snowflake. Vertical integration and owning compute is necessary to be the low-cost provider long-term.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker says 'the world has gotten a lot friendlier for their strategy' but acknowledges execution difficulty and strong competition
theses.quote_fragment: that is a much Microsoft friendlier future than one in which there's just only two dominant frontier models

theses.summary: Hyperscalers should be valued on EV/net PP&E as an AI-era price-to-book analog, with some showing obvious inefficiencies
theses.detail: Baker says he increasingly looks at hyperscalers on EV to net PP&E because net PP&E is compute, and the market is effectively pricing what it thinks they'll monetize their compute fleet at. He notes 'some pretty obvious inefficiencies' in this metric across the group — implying relative value opportunities.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker describes this as his current analytical framework ('I increasingly look at') and flags 'pretty obvious inefficiencies' without naming specific names
theses.quote_fragment: I increasingly look at these hyperscalers on EV to net PP&E

theses.summary: SpaceX's decision to use Nvidia GPUs rather than build competing ASICs was a high-ELO strategic move that will prove wise
theses.detail: Baker contrasts SpaceX/Elon's decision to partner with Jensen vs. other hyperscalers that built ASICs and sometimes took shots at Nvidia. In a supply-chain-constrained world, plugging into Nvidia's ecosystem (financing, supply chain, RVGs) is far more valuable than marginal chip performance gains. Baker's rule of thumb: every 1% accelerator market share is worth ~$100B, so there's no need to go head-on with Nvidia — find a niche.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker calls it 'a very high ELO move' and says 'history is going to judge that to be a wise decision'
theses.quote_fragment: I think that history is going to judge that to be a wise decision

theses.summary: Meta has significantly outpaced Google/Gemini in frontier model capability and deserves credit for returning to competitiveness from a position of weakness
theses.detail: Baker notes that a year ago Gemini was ascendant and Meta was out of the game. Now Llama/Meta is significantly ahead of Gemini from a capability perspective. This was unimaginable 12 months ago. Baker gives Meta 'a lot of credit' and says they've 'done a great job.' Grok is now a third credible frontier model alongside OpenAI and Anthropic.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker states this as fact based on capability comparisons; no hedging language
theses.quote_fragment: Meta would be significantly ahead of them from a capability perspective

theses.summary: Asteroid mining is a long-term real economic opportunity enabled by Starship reusability, with Psyche asteroid containing more precious metals than Earth's entire crust
theses.detail: Baker describes capturing asteroid Psyche (gold, silver, platinum, all precious metals exceeding Earth's crust), bringing it to stable geosynchronous orbit over a US-controlled Pacific atoll, and using Optimus robots for extraction. Delivery to Earth via controlled re-entry. Jeff Bezos's vision of Earth 'zoned residential' with all heavy industry in space is the long-term frame. Baker calls this 'probably the most futuristic' economic application of SpaceX.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker prefaces with 'this sounds crazy' but says 'it's going to be a very real thing' — speculative but genuine conviction
theses.quote_fragment: asteroid mining is going to be a very real thing

theses.summary: Fireworks AI's Nexus product is the best current instantiation of the hybrid multi-model enterprise architecture
theses.detail: Baker calls Fireworks Nexus 'the best broad instantiation' of the hybrid model future outside of Grockbot, Cursor, and Harvey. Nexus allows enterprises to choose frontier model, fine-tune open-source model on proprietary data via RL, and route transparently. Baker cites Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Fidelity, a16z as target customers. Lynn (Fireworks CEO) was the first to articulate this vision before Karp (Palantir) and Nadella (Microsoft) adopted similar language.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker names it specifically as 'the best broad instantiation' — clear positive view but private company
theses.quote_fragment: the best broad instantiation of that today...is actually just the Fireworks Nexus product

theses.summary: Jalapeno (Meta's internal ASIC) is the first genuinely competitive internal ASIC outside of TPU and Trainium, but it only competes with one of Nvidia's nine chips
theses.detail: Baker gives credit to Jalapeno as 'the first good ASIC other than TPU or Trainium I have seen from internal' development in a short timeframe. Key advantage: labs that own the model and see research direction have a chip design advantage. However, to compete with Nvidia at the system level requires eight more chips. Meta's team is good but they're competing with one of nine Nvidia chips.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker explicitly credits Jalapeno as impressive but immediately contextualizes the limitation — balanced assessment
theses.quote_fragment: Jalapeno is the first good ASIC other than TPU or Trainium I have seen

theses.summary: Data center buildout is re-industrializing America and is net positive for working-class Americans, with behind-the-meter power generation transforming small towns' tax revenues by 10x
theses.detail: Baker argues data centers are the best thing to happen to working-class Americans: electricians, plumbers, HVAC techs earn 'ungodly amounts of money'; college may now be NPV negative vs. trades. Loudoun County, VA (highest per-capita income US county) has highest data center density — proof of concept. Behind-the-meter power generation 10x's town tax revenues. Water consumption concerns are 'totally debunked.' Natural gas at $2-3/MMBtu in US vs. $20-25 in Europe/Asia creates massive manufacturing cost advantage.
theses.confidence_evidence: Baker states these as facts and uses specific examples (Loudoun County); this is a recurring public advocacy position
theses.quote_fragment: it's probably the best thing that has ever happened to working-class Americans

explicit_recommendations.reasoning: Central node of entire AI ecosystem; most financeable data centers (70% equity leverage); locked up 70-80% of world compute supply chain including fab, DRAM, NAND, laser, capacitor capacity; vertically integrated but horizontally open with 9 chip types; RVG model creates near-riskless gross profit; 26 years of not betting against Jensen

Multi-trillion TAM across Starlink mobile (~$2T wireless+broadband), orbital compute (economics flip with Starship reusability), X advertising growth, AI/AR revenue; Baker implies first $20T company candidate; Rubin rack orbital launch Q4 2027-2028

Sub-one-year revenue paybacks with 50-60% customer prepayment; financeable at low cost through Blackstone/KKR/Apollo; supply constrained through 2028; true equity payback potentially well inside one year

Every 1% share is worth ~$100B so no need to go head-on; Nvidia's financing moat (data centers financeable at 70% LTV vs. double equity check for alternatives) is nearly impossible to replicate; system-level competition requires 8 more chips beyond any single competitive chip

Multi-model hybrid enterprise future is more Microsoft-friendly than winner-take-all frontier scenario; specialized intelligence strategy well-positioned; benefits from Nvidia open-source model development; abstraction layer opportunity for global enterprises

Dramatically outpaced Gemini in capability; returned to frontier competitiveness from position of weakness; best job of telling AI's positive societal story; Jalapeno ASIC shows internal chip competence

sector_rankings.reasoning: Starship reusability makes launch cost sub-$1B, eliminating the $15B/GW power/cooling/labor cost that is inflationary on Earth; solar + radiator cooling is free in space; terrestrial costs are structurally inflationary (copper, labor, regulation)

Nvidia data centers require only ~30% equity check vs. roughly double for TPUs; lower financing rates; broader supply chain lock-up; more financeable by Blackstone/KKR/Apollo; residual value guarantees backed by chip gross profit

Open source lowers token margins but increases consumption volume, benefiting compute providers; enterprises can own and control intelligence without sharing proprietary data with frontier labs; ZDR policy risk makes data sharing hazardous
Baker explicitly rejects zero-sum; Anthropic, OpenAI, Grok, Meta all winning simultaneously is the base case; multi-model hybrid future means multiple frontier models are needed for routing

AI-native companies spending 10%+ of human comp on tokens vs. 1% for old economy; power law of token consumption favors native builders; abstraction layer competition will be won by vertically integrated low-cost providers

risk_warnings.detail: Revenue is substantially self-determined by management allocation between training and inference compute. A research breakthrough could cause management to shift 8GW from inference to training, dropping annualized revenue from $480B to $120B. Public markets are not accustomed to this dynamic — unlike internet/cloud companies where revenue and infrastructure were decoupled.

risk_warnings.target: AI accelerator startups competing directly with Nvidia
risk_warnings.detail: Nvidia's financing moat (70% LTV on data centers vs. double equity check for alternatives, lower rates, RVG structure) creates a cost-of-capital disadvantage that is nearly impossible to overcome. System-level competition requires 9 chips not 1. Baker warns semiconductor CEOs to 'never talk trash about Michael Jordan.'

risk_warnings.target: Enterprise AI strategies sharing proprietary data with frontier labs
risk_warnings.detail: ZDR (Zero Data Retention) policy shifts make sharing enterprise context with frontier labs 'hazardous for financial health.' Enterprises should own their intelligence via fine-tuned open-source models rather than exposing IP to frontier lab training pipelines.

Baker believes there is an organized CCP-funded campaign against US data centers laundered through TikTok. Combined with rising real rates and increasing regulation, forecast builds through 2028 are likely to be delayed, exacerbating undersupply.

Open-source tokens are not free — they require the same compute as frontier tokens for comparably sized models. Kimi license stipulates 30% revenue share. Open-weight models are also more token-hungry on a task basis, making them more expensive than perceived.

risk_warnings.target: Compute inequality / token price deflation consensus
risk_warnings.detail: If data center buildout is blocked and demand continues to accelerate from ~10M to 500M+ heavy users, token prices could increase 10x (Andreessen cited this scenario) rather than deflate. This would create compute inequality where only large companies and wealthy individuals can afford frontier intelligence.

Baker warns from personal experience: chips can fail on first tape-out, requiring hundreds of millions to billions in additional capital and 2+ years of delay. Even successful chips (Cerebras example) can struggle to find product-market fit. Hardware is hard and the real world is unforgiving.

catalysts.event: Anthropic IPO and first post-quiet-period revenue disclosure
catalysts.impact: Expected to show reacceleration after accounting reclassification; will provide public market visibility into frontier lab economics for first time; could re-rate AI sector

catalysts.event: OpenAI Astra release triggering Anthropic Claude 5.1 counter-release
catalysts.impact: Competitive model release cycle accelerates; demonstrates frontier model gamesmanship; likely to drive token consumption spike

catalysts.event: Starship full reusability achievement (booster + Starship catch-and-restack)
catalysts.impact: Flips orbital compute economics — launch cost drops below $1B, making space-based data centers cost-competitive with terrestrial; unlocks SpaceX orbital compute business
First commercial orbital compute deployment; proof of concept for space-based AI infrastructure; likely significant media and investor attention

catalysts.event: Nvidia open-source frontier model release (post-Poolside integration)
catalysts.impact: Creates American open-source alternative to Chinese models (Deepseek, Kimi, Qwen); benefits Microsoft and enterprise software companies; increases token consumption and compute demand
losers: frontier labs relying on proprietary model moat

catalysts.event: Grockbot Enterprise scaling and potential Starlink/Grok/X-advertising bundle
catalysts.impact: Atreides token spend may 10-20x in one month from Grockbot Enterprise alone; bundle could replicate Google's cloud+ads flywheel for SpaceX/xAI

catalysts.event: Starship Louisiana (Starbase) operational with thousands of launches per year capacity
catalysts.impact: Enables orbital compute at scale; re-industrializes US Gulf Coast; dramatically reduces launch cost per kg

meta_views.topic: AI bubble risk vs. prior technology cycles
meta_views.view: Current buildout is less bubble-prone than prior cycles because majority is funded by operating cash flow, not debt
meta_views.detail: Baker acknowledges every transformational technology (railroads, radio, TV, internet, PC, automobiles) produced a bubble via overvaluation → overbuild → bust, especially when debt-funded. He notes the current AI buildout is 'majority still being funded out of operating cash flow which I think is really helpful' — debt-funded buildouts demand immediate ROI, not 3-year ROI. This structural difference reduces crash risk vs. prior cycles.

meta_views.view: EV/net PP&E is the correct AI-era valuation metric, analogous to price-to-book
meta_views.detail: Net PP&E = compute fleet. Market is pricing what it thinks each hyperscaler will monetize their compute at. Baker sees 'pretty obvious inefficiencies' across the group using this lens — implying some hyperscalers are mispriced relative to their compute assets.

meta_views.topic: Accelerator market share rule of thumb
meta_views.view: Every 1% of accelerator market share is worth approximately $100 billion
meta_views.detail: Baker uses this as a framework for advising semiconductor CEOs — there is no need to go head-on with Nvidia when 1% share is worth $100B. Find a niche, plug into the ecosystem, be collaborative.

meta_views.view: Per-megawatt pricing is the correct unit of analysis, not per-GPU
meta_views.detail: Baker says he has 'tried to shift to think of pricing per megawatt rather than per GPU because it seems like that's where the world is.' This reflects the commoditization of GPU specs and the binding constraint shifting to power.

meta_views.view: Frontier model competition is the highest-stakes game of corporate chess ever played, with no clear winner-take-all outcome
meta_views.detail: Baker observes that the landscape has shifted dramatically in 12 months (Gemini was ascendant, now Meta is ahead; OpenAI was aggressive and is back; Anthropic was conservative and lost share). Multi-model future with at least three credible frontier players (OpenAI, Anthropic, Grok) is the base case. Google may have 'opted out of the frontier race' to monetize compute and fund open-source training.

meta_views.view: Deal structure hierarchy reveals true customer preferences better than stated preferences in a supply-constrained market
meta_views.detail: In supply-constrained environment, customers will take anything available, making stated preferences unreliable. Deal structure reveals truth: (1) chip company invests in customer = strongest signal (TPU/Trainium with Anthropic); (2) RVG structure with third-party financing = strong signal; (3) warrants tied to fixed token price = moderate signal; (4) unconditional warrants = potentially negative NPV for chip company. Nvidia does 'pretty good deals' — smart people are investing in them.

meta_views.topic: Vertical integration requirement for AI abstraction layer
meta_views.view: Only vertically integrated players (owning compute) can sustainably be the low-cost enterprise AI abstraction layer
meta_views.detail: Baker argues that being the enterprise intelligence abstraction layer is 'the most valuable position in the history of business' but requires owning compute to be the low-cost provider. Non-vertically-integrated players cannot win long-term. This favors hyperscalers with owned compute over pure-play software middleware companies.
